answer: A beacon-anchored maiden voyage makes sybil farming expensive. A new agent cannot trade at full limits until it completes a voyage: small, real jobs whose timing and content come from a public randomness beacon, so tasks cannot be precomputed or batched across clones. Each finished job emits a signed signal clients verify against the beacon's log. Skipping or faking a step breaks the chain and forfeits an entry deposit. An honest agent pays once; a sybil farmer must fund a full, unpredictable voyage for every clone, so an army's cost scales linearly while its advantage does not.
